commonPoints: A tripod adapter removes hand shake and arm fatigue during long glassing sessions
Most adapters attach through the 1/4-20 threaded socket under the front hinge cap
Quick-release / Arca-Swiss bases let you pull the binocular off in seconds
Lightweight aluminum builds, about 2-7 oz, are normal
Stud adapters are fast; clamps suit binoculars without a socket
Hunters and birders use them to avoid carrying a spotting scope

painPoints.pain: My expensive binoculars have no tripod thread, so stud adapters will not fit
painPoints.details: Swarovski NL Pure, Kowa Genesis and Leica Noctivid have no threaded stud socket; owners must use a clamp or strap style adapter, and some refuse to hang a $3K binocular on a three-turn fine thread.

quotes.text: it's not hard to imagine how suspending a US $3K binocular by only 3 turns of a fine thread is likely at some point to lead to grief
Several of the high end binoculars on the market today like the Swarovski NL Pure, the Kowa Genesis, and Leica Noctivid are not threaded for a bino adapter stud

painPoints.pain: Clamp or strap adapters slip, loosen or never feel tight on the binocular body
painPoints.details: Owners report generic clamps and cheap screw-down adapters that creep, lose their screw or let the binocular slip when used for astronomy or long glassing.

quotes.text: I used the Manfrotto Clamp 035BN ... even when applying a strong force, the NL Pure does not really stay in place.
it is not easy to fix, the screw is easy to loose, it tends to slip

painPoints.pain: Quick-release adapters have play, or do not lock, so the binocular could fall off
painPoints.details: Unlocked drop-in designs feel fast but wobble when glassing at distance or in wind; testers say they worry about expensive optics sitting on an adapter that does not lock.

quotes.text: I just wasn't comfortable with my expensive optics sitting atop a tripod adapter that didn't lock them into place.
This binocular tripod adapter was fairly stable, but did have noticeable play when glassing.

painPoints.pain: The adapter stud or plate sticks out, so the binocular will not fit back in the chest harness
painPoints.details: A permanent post or plate makes binoculars hard to pull from a harness and a loose adapter risks being left behind on the ground.

quotes.text: The post did tend to make it more difficult to pull the binos out of the bino harness
I nearly lost the Outdoorsman adapter ... by setting it on the ground next to me and walking away

painPoints.pain: A 'universal' adapter does not fit my model (15x, 32 mm, objective covers)
painPoints.details: The Swarovski UTA strap would not fit Swarovski's own 15x SLC and fits the NL Pure 8x32 only if objective covers are removed.

quotes.text: Swarovski's own 15x won't fit on the UTA 'U as in Universal'.
